### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **168** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**68** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **26** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `63a17b02f01bf95670c9d60b948a29e447d88ebe` — the merge of head `fe2cb2045493f31bcf6854b9415c48d617274a01` into base `8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 63a17b02f01bf95670c9d60b948a29e447d88ebe && git checkout 63a17b02f01bf95670c9d60b948a29e447d88ebe
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d fe2cb2045493f31bcf6854b9415c48d617274a01 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d && git merge --no-ff fe2cb2045493f31bcf6854b9415c48d617274a01

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8523ef9ac7c27bb05bc280b492d8e9ca5da5910d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fe2cb2045493f31bcf6854b9415c48d617274a01`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/crypto-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signed-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/seed.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/canonical.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-checkpoint.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-amendment.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-signing-key.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/sys-secret-rewrap.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/local-crypto-provider.test.ts

Inputs read: card #31908 body and all 11 comments (claim 6759393778 and its amendments, takeover and round-2 rulings 6764440313, amendment 6765374453, dev reports through 6766849305); PR #32184 body, its 36-file list and the net diff at this head; ADR-0154 on `main`; the 67 check-runs on this head (56 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed or cancelled). The rest of the diff (tests, `jcs.ts`, `merkle.ts`, `audit-writers.ts`, the other cli files, generated JSON, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Six new `@objectstack/spec/contracts` exports** — right. `IAuditCheckpointSigner`, `IAuditCheckpointSink`, `AuditCheckpointSignature`, `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry`, `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_SERVICE`, `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SINK_SERVICE`: exactly the names ruled in 6762115714, no seventh. `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` carry the same six. Slot strings equal ADR-0154 D11's `audit.checkpointSigner` and `audit.checkpointSink`. A slot constant beside its contract has precedent in spec (`CLOUD_BINDING_SERVICE`, `EMBEDDER_SERVICE`).
- **`CRYPTO_CONTEXT_SCOPES` gains `audit_seal`** — right, a widening. `LocalCryptoProvider` validates a scope against this closed set, so a context `main` refuses with `CryptoContextScopeError` is now sealed; nothing `main` accepts is refused. The type-level cost is real and declared: an exhaustive Record over `CryptoContextScope` stops compiling until it gains the member. The one in-repo site (`rewrapByScope`) is now derived from the set.
- **`rotateKey` MUST keep the id under `audit_seal`** — right, not a narrowing. The requirement attaches to a scope no provider was handed before. ADR-0154 D2 offers exactly this arm ("a contract change it declares, pinned against every shipped provider"). The pin is in `local-crypto-provider.test.ts` over every scope, and the rewrap executor's `next.id !== row.id` refusal already holds on `main`.
- **`PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` gains three names** — right as a widening, with one accepted bend (④ n6). Read in the live tree:
  - `stack.zod.ts` now accepts an action whose `objectName` is one of the three (refused on `main`); a target no loaded package registers is still refused at boot.
  - `validate-object-references` resolves them at rung ③.
  - `resolvePrimaryDatasource` intersects the registry with what is registered, so an unregistered name does not vote.
  - `organization-ownership-apply` skips a `column-drop` table that is not physically present.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-audit` root gains four names and no object** — right. The root does not re-export `objects/index.ts`, and `audit-plugin.ts` registers an explicit four-object list, so the three new objects are defined and unregistered as the changeset says.
- **`SECRET_REFERENCE_FAMILIES` gains `audit-seal`** — right. In this release every runtime takes the unregistered-holder path: one extra read of `sys_secret (id, namespace, key)`, enumerated-empty unless a row matches the producer's predicate. A false match fails closed (a gap), and no existing producer vocabulary reaches the predicate's shape.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agrees with ①; PR body and changeset carry the same line.

- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No authorable key, value or metadata type moves. A registry addition is `none` by this repository's own precedent (the `sys_trusted_key` and `sys_personal_view` changesets).
- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli` matches AGENTS.md ("`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`").
- `@objectstack/service-settings` has a test-only change and correctly no entry.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Inventory file beyond the claim** — answered by claim amendment 6765374453. The row block is the registry's own consequence, and the apply path is safe for a table that does not exist.
- **n1's behaviour (a non-canonical key leaves the family `enumerated`, not a gap)** — answered by the takeover ruling's own words ("answers `false` instead of throwing"). A key `checkpointSeedContext` cannot build is not evidence of this producer.
- **No second `main` merge** — accepted. Every check-run on this head is success or skipped; the merge queue re-tests.
- **Translations and ruling 3d's pin deferred to P1b** — accepted. Both need registration or the sealer; they are P1b acceptance items.
- **Open question 1** (`canonicalValue` pass-through) — ruled A, widened, in 6764440313; lands in P1b.
- **Open question 2** (KMS `rotateKey` pin) — ruled A, `carrier: cloud`. The PR's acceptance notes name the MUST and the widened union; delivering that note to the cloud lane is the seat's at landing.
- **`sign()` re-sign loop pin** — ruled to P1b (S1). This head documents the duty only.
- **Round-1 record 6763138129** (M1, S1–S5), as the takeover states it, is met on this head: the registry rows, the `sign` duty, the sink body's contents, `checkpoint_sequence`, four producers in the crypto docs, and "defined, not yet registered" in the changeset.

Nothing escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix and no should-fix. Seven nits; none changes behaviour on this head.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts`** — holds.
- Against ADR-0154 D6 and D11: the signer returns the key id with the signature; `trustedPublicKey` is the trust anchor D9's live check needs and never reads a row's word; the sink is handed a record after it is signed and stored, and its failure does not stop sealing.
- Against `signed-body.ts`: both bodies carry `signing_key_id` inside the signed bytes, so the caller's duty as written is the only sound use of the ruled shape. A signature whose `keyId` differs from the bytes' can never verify.
- Tried to break "the body exactly as signed" as an object rather than bytes: every body member is a string, null, a safe integer, or an array or object of those (`fencing_token` is deliberately decimal text), so an independent RFC 8785 writer reproduces the bytes.
- **n2 (nit).** The "what a sink receives" list reads as complete and is not. The bodies also carry `kind`, `leaf_count`, `canon_version`, `fencing_token`, `signing_key_id`, and the instants `sealed_at`, `sealed_through` and `amended_at`. None is a value, salt, seed or key material, so the classification statement stands. Complete the list when the file is next touched (P1b).

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/crypto-provider.ts`** — holds. Sentence by sentence against `seed.ts` and the object files:
- namespace is the sealed object's name and key is `JCS([organization id or null, sequence])` — `checkpointSeedContext` ✓
- namespace `sys_audit_signing_key` and key the fingerprint — `signingKeyContext` ✓
- no `tenantId` in either context ✓
- holders `sys_audit_checkpoint.seed_handle` and `sys_audit_signing_key.private_handle` exist under those names and equal `AUDIT_SEAL_SECRET_HOLDERS` ✓
- **n1 (nit).** The scope list says "Both are referenced from inside signed bodies". Only the seed's handle is (`CheckpointSignedBody.seed_handle`). The signing key's private handle sits in the unsigned `sys_audit_signing_key.private_handle`; signed bodies name the key by fingerprint. The MUST itself is right for both, because nothing rewrites either holder (ADR-0154 D2 last bullet). Correct the reason in P1b.
- **n3 (nit, a P1b acceptance item).** A seed's `ctx.key` is recorded in `sys_secret.key`, which `main` declares `maxLength: 128` and keys by index, so it is a `varchar(128)`. This slice bounds `chain_key` at 259 on the stated premise that an organization id may be 255 characters. Such an id gives a seed key of about 260 characters, which does not fit. Nothing writes a seed on this head, and real ids are far shorter. P1b's sealer must either refuse a coordinate that exceeds the holder's bound before the write, or the bound is raised, with a pin either way.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts`** — holds. One barrel line; the generated surfaces agree.

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`** — holds against its conformance test, which scans declared `*.object.ts` files and so requires the three names once the files exist.
- **n6 (nit, accepted deviation).** The module's contract says each group is "the exact set that package registers". Until P1b the `plugin-audit` group lists three objects nothing registers. The new group comment says so; the seat chose this over moving the object files (6765374453); the PR's acceptance notes name the consequence. It closes when P1b registers them. A release cut between P1a and P1b ships the bend.

**Implementing files.**
- `signed-body.ts` — agrees with ADR-0154 D4 field for field, with D7 (the checkpoint named by signed `checkpoint_sequence` in the chain the body already names, per S3) and with D8. An absent `tenant_id` is refused; a stated NULL is the deployment chain; `previous_digest` is null exactly at sequence 0.
  - **n4 (nit).** `amendmentBodyFromRow` reads only its own kind's columns, so a redaction row may carry non-null expiry columns (or the reverse) under a valid signature. The object's docblock says `id`, `chain_key` and `signature` are the only columns outside the signed body. Have the P2 verifier refuse a stored amendment whose other-kind columns are not NULL, beside its `chain_key` agreement check.
- `seed.ts` — agrees. The salt is `HMAC-SHA-256(seed, object ‖ 0x00 ‖ id ‖ 0x00 ‖ column)`; the predicate is total.
- `canonical.ts` — agrees with D1.
  - **n7 (nit, under ruled open question 1).** The `date` rule reads a `Date` in UTC and keeps the first ten characters. A driver that hands a date column back as local midnight would canonicalise to the previous day east of UTC. No `date` column is sealed today. P1b's per-type rule must pin `date` against what `driver-sql` returns per dialect, or refuse a `Date` under `date`.
- The three object files — agree with the bodies and with D4 and D6: `append-only`, private, get and list only, a global unique `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)`.
- `secret-reference-union.ts` and `sys-secret-rewrap.ts` — agree with producer 4 as the contract states it. The rewrap writes by the row's id and refuses a re-id before any write.
  - **n5 (nit, prose).** The family's header says a missed row would be unverifiable "after a master-key change". `os secret rewrap` on `main` re-seals only rows of an older AAD derivation and changes no master key; the changeset's "re-wraps the sealer's secrets" has the same reach. Separately, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` still says `sys_secret` "is written by three producers" and that both commands read "all three holder families". The refusal now prints "of 4". Fix on the prose face, here or with P1b, when the sealer first writes these rows.
- `organization-ownership-inventory.ts` — the three rows are right (`systemFields.tenant: false`, nothing to drop).
- `local-crypto-provider.test.ts` — pins the MUST against the one shipped provider under every scope.

Carried to later slices: n1, n2, n3 and n7 to P1b; n4 to P2; n5 on the prose face; n6 closes at P1b registration.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：ADR-0154 第一片（P1a），接手 #32100 并按第二轮评审改完。审计封存的纯计算核心（规范 JSON、行的规范形、加盐承诺、种子派生盐、Merkle 树、签名体），三个新平台对象（检查点、修订、签名密钥，已定义未注册），spec 的 `audit_seal` 加密作用域与签名器/投递两个接缝契约，`sys_secret` 引用并集的第 4 族 `audit-seal`。本轮新增：三个对象登记进平台对象注册表（修好 CI 红），脱敏修订改为按检查点的已签名序号引用检查点。
- 为什么改：后面的封存器和 `os audit verify` 都建在这层上；第 4 族保证 `os secret rewrap` 会重包封存器的种子与私钥，孤儿清扫也不会把它们当成无人引用。
- 风险与回滚：这一片什么都不封存，三个对象也没注册到任何运行时。运行行为只变两处：引用并集多一族、rewrap 报告多一个 `audit_seal` 计数；另外 `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` 多了三个名字。回滚就是整体 revert。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signed-body.ts`（核验依赖的签名字节，本轮改了 `checkpoint_sequence` 和缺列拒收），`packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts`（签名器调用方义务、投递方收到什么），`packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts` 的第 4 族。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/audit-seal`（预期 36 个测试全绿），再跑 `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test:repo`（预期 `platform-object-names.test.ts` 绿）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。P1b 到 P4 合入前，cloud 不要给 `sys_ai_audit_log` 加封存 opt-in。

席位意见：ACCEPT。速读六行与我读的 diff 一致，不改。契约复核在 CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER 档 PASS（comment 6767050949，`Head-sha` fe2cb204，0 must-fix / 0 should-fix / 7 nit）。spec 面之外的部分由本席按 TIER_DEFAULT 核对，见下。

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `fe2cb2045493f31bcf6854b9415c48d617274a01`

1. **Shape.** 36 files, +2506/-43, under 3000. Slice P1a round 2 of #31908 is `Part of`, never `Fixes`: P1b–P4 remain. It supersedes closed #32100. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on both the body and the changeset, and agree with the claim and the record's ②. The file surface matches the takeover claim 6764440313 plus amendment 6765374453 (the cli inventory).
2. **Premises measured (remainder, TIER_DEFAULT).**
   - `jcs.ts` serialises per RFC 8785: sorted member names, `JSON.stringify` numbers and strings, and it refuses non-finite numbers, unpaired surrogates and non-plain objects.
   - `merkle.ts` promotes an odd last node, which gives the RFC 6962 root for every leaf count (left-balanced split). It refuses an empty list or a non-32-byte leaf.
   - `audit-writers.ts` keeps the three seal objects out of the ledger (no seal-of-a-seal loop).
   - `rewrapByScope` is derived from `CRYPTO_CONTEXT_SCOPES`, and the orphan refusal counts `SECRET_REFERENCE_FAMILIES.length`.
   - The plugin root exports four seed helpers and no object, so nothing is registered.
3. **Gates (check-runs at fe2cb204).** 67 in total: 56 success, 11 skipped (path-scheduled or opt-in), 0 failed. `mergeable_state` is clean. K = 0 (PRBASE `8523ef9a` is current `origin/main`). Generated `os-regen` paths are in the diff (`api-surface`, `export-origins`, `platform-object-tenancy-census.json`), and they are current against a base with K = 0. The merge group re-tests them.

   - There is no second main merge.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [42815891188](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42815891188) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Build & E2E UI](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42815891188/job/129831939408)** — 失败步骤: check:eager-closure — weigh the Console's eager closure against its budget（日志不可读，点进 job 看）

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
